articles.title: ‘Throw your medals in the bin,’ Roy Keane tells Manchester City players
articles.summary: ‘They won the titles because cheating was going on’ Micah Richards says he is ‘devastated and heartbroken’ Former Manchester United captain Roy Keane said he would throw the “medals in the bin” if he were a Manchester City player following Premier League confirmation on Tuesday that the club were…
body: City, who continue to deny any wrongdoing, won eight trophies, including three Premier League titles between 2009 and 2018, the period under investigation. Keane said the achievements of City’s players had become redundant because of the “cheating” that took place during that time.

“If I was a player, I’d be 100% sticking those medals in the bin. Of course you would, it’s cheating,” the ITV football pundit stated during the coverage of England’s match against the Czech Republic in the Nations League. “They won it on the pitch because cheating was going on.” And on the club he added: “They knew it would hurt a lot of people, but they’ve still done it.”

Meanwhile, the former City defender Micah Richards says the damning verdict on the club has left him devastated and heartbroken. City were found to have engaged in an almost £1bn scheme to either inflate revenues or reduce costs through a series of “sham” arrangements in order to avoid breaching league and Uefa financial regulations.
Speaking on The Rest is Football podcast, Richards said: “The reports were troubling. I saw the words which were used by the Premier League in sham contracts and I felt absolutely devastated.

articles.title: Jameis Winston is now the New York Giants’ starter. He’s far from a goofball hero though
articles.summary: The quarterback is widely adored on and off the field. Whether he deserves the public spotlight is another question. Throughout the NFL’s history, we’ve had our fair share of clown princes. Not too long ago, Rob Gronkowski was the league’s court jester.
body: There’s probably something deeply insightful to say about the need for goofballs in a sport characterized by militarized order and a seriousness that borders on self-parody, but what’s important now is how we reflect on these chosen merrymakers.

The current clown prince is Jameis Winston, who has become the New York Giants’ starting quarterback after a brutal knee injury to Jaxson Dart. Though the Giants have traded for former Vikings first-round pick and third-string quarterback JJ McCarthy, all indications at the moment are that Winston will continue to start.

Winston’s persona has always been goofy. His 2015 fumble against Oregon in the Rose Bowl was itself an act of unintentional comedy; a Heisman winner who couldn’t help but stumble backwards and flop like a beached whale.

That was the culmination of an up-and-down but nevertheless winning season at Florida State, after which the Tampa Bay Buccaneers selected him with the No 1 overall pick in the NFL draft. At the time, Buccaneers general manager Jason Licht praised Winston’s leadership and football character, doubling down on that in 2017 by adding that Winston was “the best leader I think I’ve ever been around – in anything”.

Whether he deserves the public spotlight is another question.

articles.title: Will Pocognoli change goalkeeper after Swiss loss?
articles.summary: Andy Burke ponders whether Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli will change goalkeeper after Angus Gunn's performance in the 3-0 defeat by Switzerland.
body: If it was a bad night for Jack Hendry, whose 11th-minute red card precipitated Scotland's demise against Switzerland, then it was hardly an evening Angus Gunn will look back on with any great fondness either.
"I've never been a big defender of goalkeepers and I'm looking for more from Angus Gunn," was the view of Sportsound pundit Andy Halliday on the Scotland keeper's performance.

The San Jose Earthquakes stopper, 30, was arguably at fault for the first and third of the three goals that hit the back of his net as the Swiss coasted to victory at Hampden in a deeply unsatisfactory first home match under Sebastien Pocognoli.

The opening goal came in the immediate aftermath of Hendry's red card for denying Dan Ndoye a goalscoring opportunity. Scotland thought they had been given a reprieve as referee Nenad Minakovic's original award of a penalty was changed after a VAR review to a free-kick on the edge of the box.

articles.summary: Plus: European stadiums with low Google ratings, losing hat-tricks and the last time Spain had less than 50% possession. Mail us with your all of your questions and answers.
body: “Jamie Spencer, 17, made his first first-team appearance in a competitive match, for Huddersfield at Doncaster on 9 September in the prestigious EFL Trophy,” emails Richard Askham. “He came on as a substitute in the 66th minute and scored with his second touch of the ball, one to control it and the second to score. Has anyone scored with their very first touch, which is the only way to better young Spencer’s achievement?”

We covered a variation of this question back in 2021, with answers on players scoring with their first touch on debut for their new clubs. This week, though, goes a step further, covering players that score with the first touches of their professional careers, although there are a few answers from that 2021 piece that work here, too: Jack Aitchison for Celtic in 2016, Matt Hatch for Central Coast Mariners in 2021, England one-cap wonder Michael Ricketts for Walsall against Brighton in 1996, Maheta Molango (now the chief executive of the Professional Footballers’ Association) for Brighton against Reading in August 2004, and Yan Dhanda for Swansea City at Sheffield United in 2018.

articles.title: Dropping Kelly and Toone could prove a World Cup masterstroke by Wiegman | Tom Garry
articles.summary: England’s coach has given a wake-up call to her whole squad by leaving out two heroes of 2022 and 2025. Sarina Wiegman sent a clear message to two of England’s biggest names on Tuesday and – in doing so, irrespective of reputations – fired the same warning to every player: perform for your club or…
body: Wiegman was unequivocal with her reasoning for leaving Ella Toone and Chloe Kelly out of her squad for October’s playoff against Greece. Her straight-to-the-point and typically honest style made it inescapably clear, when she said: “The main reason is that I think the levels weren’t what I expect from them on the pitch.”

Amid reports of Kelly struggling with an injury, Wiegman was asked to clarify if any concerns about fitness had played a part in her decision and she said: “Well, I had a conversation with Chloe and, for me, it was just what I saw on the pitch, so I kept it [to the] football.”

With those blunt words, the Dutchwoman emphasised that she was picking her squad on form, and it is a message that has an extra urgency given there are just under nine months to go until the start of the World Cup, which England will attempt to qualify for over the next 10 weeks across two rounds of playoffs, starting with October’s tie against Greece, and ultimately seek to go one better than 2023’s second-placed finish.

articles.title: Sheedy surprised as header goes viral
articles.summary: Cardiff fly-half Callum Sheedy says he did not realise his "header" against Scarlets in the United Rugby Championship (URC) game would go viral.
body: Sheedy headed the ball forward after chasing his own kick in the second half of the 21-15 victory against Scarlets on Saturday night.
"I probably wasn't thinking at the time, that was the problem," said Sheedy.
"I remember the ball sitting up, and I could see Blair [Murray] coming towards me, and I thought it was going be an aerial contest.
"I thought there needed to be a way of me getting the ball past him, and there wasn't enough time to get it down to my foot, so the nearest body part was my head.

articles.title: Fishlock set for Wales return - but not as player
articles.summary: Rhian Wilkinson says icon Jess Fishlock will be back with the national team if they reach a World Cup play-off final in December – but only as a coach.
body: Fishlock, Wales' most-capped footballer, called time on her international career last October.

But the 39-year-old continues to shine for Seattle Reign, having claimed two fine goals in last weekend's win over Boston Legacy to become the National Women's Soccer League club's all-time leading scorer.

Wales, meanwhile, are without a string of senior players for the World Cup play-off semi-final against Albania next month, but Wilkinson says she has turned down Fishlock's tongue-in-cheek offer to come out of international retirement.

"There was never a doubt that Jess Fishlock could still do a job for us. [But] I think it was absolutely the right time for her to step away after that amazing qualification for the Euro [last year]."

articles.title: Cubs’ Kevin Gausman Sends Blue Jays ‘Heartbreak’ Message After Exit
articles.summary: As the MLB playoff field prepares for October competition, the reigning American League pennant holders are left to regroup after a major disappointment. “A season that started full of hope ended in disappointment for the 2026 Toronto Blue Jays,” Sportsnet’s Ben Nicholson-Smith wrote.
body: Shortly after the season ended, numerous members of the Blue Jays have voiced their disappointment in that turn of events. And so has a key member from the 2025 run, whose own playoff pursuit is still alive now that he’s a member of the Chicago Cubs.

Veteran right-hander Kevin Gausman was traded to the Cubs at the deadline, but he hasn’t completely moved on from the team where he spent the previous five seasons, helping it reach the highest levels of the American League.

For Gausman, the end of Toronto’s season brought back some of the emotions surrounding his own departure. Reflecting on the Blue Jays’ series against the Seattle Mariners, a team they bested in the American League Championship Series last year, Gausman noted a harsh feeling in the clubhouse after his former team scored just two runs in the three-game rematch.
“There was a little bit of heartbreak there,” Gausman told The Athletic’s Mitch Bannon.

articles.title: The Premier League footballers studying to become sporting directors
articles.summary: Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall, Taiwo Awoniyi and others have been juggling education with a football career - even studying on the team bus during away trips.
body: The scene resembles an Oxbridge graduation ceremony, but those gathered in caps and gowns are in fact Premier League footballers or former players who have won major honours in Europe and around the world.
The 2026 cohort of graduates from the PFA Business School includes Everton midfielder Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall, Coventry City striker Taiwo Awoniyi and a host of well-known figures.

In the event at Arsenal's Emirates Stadium, Cesar Azpilicueta tells the group how studying on the morning of the 2021 Champions League final helped take his mind off the occasion before he captained Chelsea to a 1-0 win over Manchester City in Porto.

Dewsbury-Hall, 28, travelled by train from Merseyside to London to attend the ceremony and, despite being in the best form of his career, explains why he had completed a postgraduate diploma in global football sport directorship.

articles.title: Greenwich High School Athletic Hall of Fame to induct seven
articles.summary: The Greenwich High School Athletic Hall of Fame will induct seven athletes, coaches and contributors Oct. 23, honoring a class whose accomplishments span generations of Cardinals athletics.
body: The ceremony will take place at halftime of Greenwich's football game against New Canaan, which is scheduled for a 7 p.m. kickoff at Cardinal Stadium. A free Hall of Fame social will begin at 5:30 p.m. in the Greenwich High School Performing Arts Center Galleria.

The 2026 class includes Mike Brown, a 1976 graduate and three-sport athlete in soccer, basketball and baseball; Joe Cabrera, a 1977 graduate recognized for football and track and field; and Douglas Springer, a 1964 graduate and standout swimmer.

The class also includes former Director of Health, Physical Education and Athletics Charles Dattola; boys soccer, boys swimming and boys track and field coach Peter McDevitt; field hockey and girls basketball coach Carolyn Pagnano; and football and boys basketball coach Dave Rice. Dattola and McDevitt will be honored posthumously.

The induction marks the Hall of Fame's return after a three-year hiatus. Current Greenwich student-athletes and coaches will join alumni, families and members of the community in celebrating the honorees.

articles.title: Williams aiming to change course of Warrington's history with Grand Final victory
articles.summary: George Williams has set himself one task for when he steps out in the Super League Grand Final as Warrington Wolves skipper: Make sure he leaves the club with a trophy.
body: When Williams returned from the NRL in 2021, he made the bold decision to not go back to his hometown club of Wigan and instead headed to Warrington.
After five years there, he is poised to return to Australia and has one last opportunity to try and depart with a trophy.

It is set to be a pretty-evenly-matched Grand Final as third- and fourth-placed Warrington and Wakefield Trinity do battle. Two underdog teams who beat the first- and second-placed sides to make it to Old Trafford.

It is not lost on Williams how big this match is as he could lead Warrington to their maiden Grand Final triumph to become just the sixth team in the history of the competition to lift the Super League trophy.

articles.title: Kane on target for England, Saibari and Ndiaye with wins
articles.summary: Tuesday night saw Harry Kane and England play Czech Republic in their second UEFA Nations League match after the 3-2 opening defeat to Spain, while Ismael Saibari and Bara Sapoko Ndiaye were also in action for Morocco and Senegal respectively. fcbayern.com has the lowdown: Kane wraps up 2-0 win.
body: Bayern goal-getter Kane netted the second goal in the Three Lions’ 2-0 win over Czech Republic in Prague. The England captain netted in the 69th minute, 22 minutes after Anthony Gordon had opened the scoring and two minutes before he was replaced by Jude Bellingham.

England were however helped by an early red card for the Czechs, who were reduced to 10 men after just 25 minutes following a dangerous challenge by Pavel Sulc. The Three Lions laid siege to the Czech Republic goal after that, although Kane and others were denied by home goalkeeper Matej Kovar. The first goal after the break then broke the Czech resistance, and when Kane was left free to fire in, it was game over. England travel to Croatia next on Saturday, with kick-off at 18:00 CEST.

articles.title: Carra: Man City should be stripped of titles and have owners removed
articles.summary: Jamie Carragher believes Manchester City should be stripped of the titles they won during the years they have been found guilty of financial breaches - and says the club's owners should be removed from their positions.
body: City have been found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules by an independent commission.

The club continue to deny the breaches, with chief executive Ferran Soriano calling the process a "Premier League conspiracy theory" in a video message to players and staff. The club have confirmed they will appeal against the ruling and have until Friday October 2 to do so.
During the period between the 2009/10 season and 2017/18 season, City won three Premier League titles, one FA Cup, three League Cups and one Community Shield.
"I do think Manchester City's titles they've won in this time, or trophies, should be taken off their list," Sky Sports pundit Carragher said.

articles.title: Mind games to start today? 'Fury will try every trick in the book to get to AJ'
articles.summary: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua's first press conference is expected to go ahead in London on Wednesday ahead of their blockbuster heavyweight fight on December 11, and Sky Sports ' Matthew Macklin has spoken of what he expects when the two British rivals face off....
body: The psychological, mental aspect of boxing is huge. It's an individual sport - one on one - so if you can get into the other guy's head and help put him in a negative headspace, you're halfway there.
Confidence is key. And if someone's struggling with confidence, if you can put some seeds of doubt in their mind, that's a real benefit to you.
There's a lot on the line. A lot of people involved, a lot of money, a lot of pride, a lot of ego, so there's already cracks appearing left, right and centre.
There will be people there who will try and control things as best they can, trying to make sure that nothing physical happens. But I'd expect Fury to be animated.
